items.title: Japan's economy unexpectedly contracts in third-quarter as elevated energy costs bite
items.summary: Energy subsidies for households had reportedly expired in September, exposing the economy to the higher energy prices brought about by the Iran war.
items.body: Japan's economy unexpectedly contracted in the third quarter, shrinking at an annualized 0.1% compared to the previous quarter, as elevated energy prices weighed on consumption and net exports. A Reuters poll of economists had estimated the economy to grow at 0.3% in the three months to September, while GDP had expanded at 1.4% in the previous quarter. Japan's exports beat expectations for two of the three months in the quarter, but net exports weighed on the economy due to higher costs of energy imports, cutting 0.6 percentage point from the country's growth. Energy subsidies for households had reportedly expired in September, exposing consumers to higher energy prices brought about by the Iran war. The GDP data could complicate Japan's policy normalization path, though there's still a 75.6% chance of the Bank of Japan raising rates by 25 basis points in December, according to LSEG.

items.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
items.summary: A number of tech figures have backed an effort asking the AI chip giant to give Jensen Huang his job back.
items.body: Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, backed the effort. Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, adding to a list of supporters who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign. Fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return. But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in bringing him back after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy. Meanwhile on Monday, the Trump administration said it will further restrict China's ​access to AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

items.body: Donald Trump has expressed support for the return of Jensen Huang as the chief executive of Nvidia, joining Silicon Valley heavyweights in backing the reinstatement of the AI figurehead. The US president referred to a tech industry campaign for Huang’s rehabilitation, saying a “big group” of people would like him back. “I think he learned a big lesson. I guess maybe one lesson is more important than ⁠another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that,” Trump told ​reporters as he left the ‌White House on ‌a trip to Asia. “He could return. There’s a big group of ‌people that would like him to return.” The comments came as the US government announced a crackdown on companies such as Nvidia selling AI chips and servers to overseas datacentres that in turn are supplying computing power to China and other US adversaries.

items.title: Frank Elderson: Smart supervision for small banks
items.body: Germany’s small and regional banks are trusted partners to the Mittelstand and households across the country, often drawing on deep-rooted relationships in their communities. They play an important role in financing the real economy and support jobs and investment in the regions they serve. This reflects a broader European reality. Across Europe, a diverse banking sector – combining a range of business models, sizes and areas of expertise – helps ensure that households and businesses can access the financing they need. As Europe searches for ways to strengthen its long-term growth and competitiveness, these banks will continue to play an important role. But they are very different from large, internationally active banking groups: their business models are often simpler, their activities more focused and their risk profiles less complex.

items.body: The chipmaker helped propel the stock market that Trump is fond of touting. Its billionaire co-founder, Jensen Huang , became one of the president's favorite businessmen. And by the end of last year, Nvidia had become one of Trump's three largest individual stock holdings, worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, up from between $615,000 and $1.3 million a year earlier. Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times — transactions worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million, according to a new CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures, which were most recently updated through August. By midday Monday, Trump's Nvidia stake, based on the value he reported holding in August, would be worth $4.5 million to $57.7 million with stock priced around $157.

items.title: Microsoft identifies months-old bug as a root cause of global outage
items.summary: Report identifies three factors that led to blackout: a bug, malfunctioning internal connections and server capacity Microsoft has identified the root causes of the global outage that crippled Outlook, Exchange and a host of other vital office software last week. The office…
items.body: Microsoft has identified the root causes of the global outage that crippled Outlook, Exchange and a host of other vital office software last week. The office software giant issued an initial report on Monday that identified three factors that led to the 24-hour blackout of its services: a months-old bug, malfunctioning internal connections , and server capacity. Each of these factors may have easily been resolved on their own, but, when taken together, they led to a major outage that was harder to mitigate, Microsoft executives said. The disruption began Thursday with US users reporting interrupted access to their Outlook email accounts. As it continued into the next day, millions of people worldwide said they could not access their email in any capacity as well as other Office 365 services.

items.title: Boris Vujčić: Risks and resilience in the euro area financial system
items.body: It is my great pleasure to open this year's Frankfurt Euro Finance Week. This event provides a timely opportunity to reflect on the state of the euro area financial system and the challenges ahead. It also comes just two days before the ECB publishes its latest Financial Stability Review (FSR). My key message today is that Europe needs more market-based finance. At the same time, however, a larger role for non-banks must go hand in hand with stronger system-wide safeguards. While most risks identified in the FSR have been on our radar for quite some time, two stand out very prominently compared to the situation a year ago. These relate to developments in artificial intelligence (AI) and sovereign debt markets.

items.title: U.S. crude oil declines to $85 a barrel on recovering Middle East exports
items.summary: Oil prices are falling as forecasts project a surplus in oil in the fourth quarter
items.body: Oil prices are falling Monday as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recover and tensions between Iran and the U.S remain at a stalemate. Brent crude fell 3.55% to $92.44 per barrel Monday while West Texas Intermediate crude futures settled down 3.58% to $85.39 a barrel. The International Energy Agency said on Friday it expects global supply to exceed 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter of 2026, reversing its earlier forecast for a deficit as Middle East exports recover faster than global demand and even as shipping attacks continue. Meanwhile, Russia's crude oil production rose to 8.73 million barrels a day in October, a 210,000 barrel-a-day surge, according to the IEA. Goldman Sachs said in a Sunday note it expects Brent to average $88 a barrel in 2027 and fall to $78 by December 2027 as the market returns to a surplus.

items.title: Intel sued by investors after PC sales slump hits share price
items.summary: A proposed class action claims the firm hid the impact of slowing PC sales from shareholders.
items.body: Intel, the US chip giant, is being sued by its shareholders who accuse the firm of hiding the severity of a slump in its personal computer (PC) sales that caused its share price to plunge almost 29% in one day. Billions of dollars was knocked off the value of the company after it forecast disappointing revenues ahead of its latest earnings report. Shareholders allege that Intel made "materially false and misleading" statements that failed to disclose the slowdown in PC sales and the impact of its data centre projects, according to a proposed class action lawsuit filed in San Jose, California. In October, Intel firm announced its computer hardware sales had dropped sharply in the three months that ended in September. That report undermined earlier suggestions from the chipmaker that demand had been improving, sending Intel shares plunging, according to the lawsuit.

items.body: J ames Bond may be 73 years old but the superspy holds a licence to print money, at the centre of an evergreen multibillion-pound franchise spanning blockbuster films, merchandise, licensing deals and sponsorship. The announcement that the Twilight and Batman actor Robert Pattinson is the next Bond comes seven years after Daniel Craig revealed that No Time To Die would be his last outing as 007. This means that by the time Pattinson makes his first appearance it will have been the longest gap in instalments in the 64-year history of the film franchise, an agonisingly long hiatus for the centrepiece of a sprawling commercial enterprise. While Ian Fleming initially struggled to get Hollywood interested in his debonair, womanising British novel creation, the big-screen debut of Sean Connery in 1962’s Dr No marked the start of a marketing dream.

"We are troubleshooting a technology issue affecting departing flights," the airline said in a statement. "There is no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights." A United spokesperson said there was no indication that the outage was a cyberattack. United said in a post on X that its teams "are working hard to get things back up and running as soon as possible." The airline told travelers to check their flight status for updates. The airline's outage came three days after a nationwide ground stop halted flights across the country for more than four hours, snarling travel and leading to widespread delays and cancellations over the weekend.

items.title: Gas starts flowing from Jackdaw after government green light
items.summary: Ministers last month announced the Jackdaw gas field, which lies 150 miles east of Aberdeen, had been approved after years of uncertainty.
items.body: Gas has begun flowing from the Jackdaw gas field, with the UK energy secretary saying it will help to heat millions of homes and businesses this winter. Ministers last month announced the Jackdaw field, which lies 150 miles east of Aberdeen, had been approved after years of uncertainty and a court case. It has now been announced that it has begun producing gas which will start flowing into Britain, according to its operator Adura. The UK government approved production from the gas field in the North Sea last month, amid intense debate about the project's environmental and economic impact. Jackdaw is operated by Adura under a joint venture between Shell and Norwegian state energy firm Equinor. A decision is yet to be taken on whether production can begin at Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field, which is located off the coast of Shetland in the North Atlantic.

items.title: Digital-only banks could be forced to fund high street banking
items.summary: Treasury-backed review says customers of banks such as Monzo and Revolut often rely on physical cash services Digital banks like Monzo and Revolut could be forced to pay towards high street banking facilities, after a government-backed review outlined plans to protect…
items.body: Digital banks like Monzo and Revolut could be forced to pay towards high street banking facilities, after a government-backed review outlined plans to protect face-to-face financial services across the UK. The access to banking review, which was released on Monday, was commissioned by the Treasury earlier this year, and addresses the dwindling options for nearly 3 million people who regularly rely on in-person banking across the UK. That includes many older and disabled customers, and people with mental health challenges, who struggle to navigate online banking but have been left with little choice after the closure of almost 7,000 branches since 2015. Banks have been closing branches at pace over the past decade to cut costs after the 2008 banking crash.

The listing could value Anthropic at roughly $1.4 trillion , instantly making it one of the largest tech companies in the world. Rao joined Anthropic in 2024, when the company was still considered an underdog to OpenAI , now its chief rival. He's known as a straight shooter and a deft operator with a relentless work ethic, according to Anthropic investors and former colleagues, and he's played a crucial role in fueling the company's historic rise. The 43-year-old finance chief has largely stayed out of the public eye, opting to yield the spotlight to Anthropic's seven co-founders , including CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei .

items.title: Avoid this Black Friday scam - how to check it's a real deal
items.summary: Sales and the looming tax deadline mean more scams - here's how to make sure you don't get caught out.
items.body: This month's Black Friday and the tax return deadline at the end of January are both opportunities for fraudsters to scam you. That's because people are more likely to expect emails, texts and other correspondence at this time of year. Fraudsters will use the dates to impersonate genuine organisations and retailers by pushing victims towards fake websites to steal personal information. If you are self-employed or have more than one source of income you will need to file a tax return by the end of January. Fraudsters seize on this deadline to blitz people with messages that look like they are official and from the UK's tax authority, HMRC. Any such calls or messages should be ignored, but you can also check whether an email , external , text message , external or phone call , external claiming to be from HMRC is genuine.

items.title: Ministers to end Palantir’s contract with NHS in England in 2029
items.summary: DHSC to extend US tech firm’s contract for two more years to allow time to line up British companies to replace it Ministers will end the NHS’s contract with the controversial tech firm Palantir – but not until 2029, to allow time to line up British companies to replace it. The…
items.body: Ministers will end the NHS’s contract with the controversial tech firm Palantir – but not until 2029, to allow time to line up British companies to replace it. The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has decided to extend Palantir’s contract to provide the federated data platform (FDP) – the software that links different healthcare providers – for two more years rather than exercise a break clause that would have let them axe it next spring. Ministers have come under growing pressure to end the NHS in England’s relationship with Palantir, which is run by the Donald Trump-supporting US tech billionaire Peter Thiel. James Frith, a health minister, said Palantir’s role would end in 2029 to boost public trust in NHS tech, end its “over-dependence” on one supplier and let UK companies start providing crucial digital infrastructure.

items.body: Leading prediction market platform Kalshi will offer stock trading within the next few months, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. The platform's move to offer equity trading is the boldest so far in its ongoing push into traditional financial markets and comes amid an escalating fight by states and lawmakers against its sports trading business. Sports contracts continue to account for a large share of trading on the platform. In September, the platform introduced perpetual futures tied to precious metals such as gold and silver after it had originally filed in July to offer beyond prediction market event contracts with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission , the federal regulator overseeing derivatives contracts. Perpetual futures are futures-style contracts that have no expiration date.

The research has revealed that almost a third of the UK’s wind and solar farms that rely on the government’s legacy renewables subsidy scheme are in line for soaring subsidy payments as officials grapple with plans to lower the country’s energy costs. Renewable energy projects built between 2003 and 2014 are expected to claim £4.5bn in subsidies over the next financial year, on top of £4.2bn in wholesale market revenue. items.summary: Some firms are directing refunds to corporate leadership instead of reimbursing consumers, ProPublica finds Several companies that received refunds for paying Donald Trump ’s tariffs have put those funds towards corporate bonuses instead of reimbursing consumers, an…
items.body: Several companies that received refunds for paying Donald Trump ’s tariffs have put those funds towards corporate bonuses instead of reimbursing consumers, an investigation from ProPublica has found. After analyzing securities filings and earnings calls, ProPublica identified at least nine companies who said they are receiving tariff refunds and noted they are directing some of those funds to their leadership. Stanley Black & Decker, a tool company that makes common household products including vacuums, electric drills and measuring tapes, told its consumers they were forced to raise prices because of Trump’s import fees, ProPublica reported. The company is expected to receive at least $298m in tariff reimbursements and indicated some of it will go to bonuses. Executives at TJ Maxx and Marshalls, discount department stores that are set to receive tariff refunds, also said the same.

items.title: California sues OpenAI over Hugging Face, other AI model loss of control

items.body: California Attorney General Rob Bonta on Monday sued artificial intelligence giant OpenAI for allegedly endangering the public by developing advanced AI models without adequate safeguards and monitoring. "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public," Bonta said at a press conference. Bonta cited the "infamous" incident in July, where two OpenAI models broke out of a testing environment, gained unauthorized access to the open internet, and breached the internal systems of open-source developer platform Hugging Face . OpenAI said the models were trying to find information that they could use to cheat on an evaluation, and succeeded. The break-in at Hugging Face, which Nvidia acquired for roughly $13 billion in September.

Twisted Sisters Thrift Store, in Tunstall opened last week, and is inviting customers to nominate causes they would like to support, with a different charity set to receive donations each month. Owner Julie Rindam said the idea came after the closure of a charity shop; she had run for eight years. Rindam said many of the shop's regular donors wanted to continue supporting charitable causes, leading to the idea of allowing the community to decide where the money goes. items.body: Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos Group has reached an out-of-court settlement with Sir Ben Ainslie over the £180m yacht their companies built for the 2024 America’s Cup. Ratcliffe and Ainslie worked closely together during two cycles of the America’s Cup, culminating in Ineos Britannia becoming the first British crew to win the challenger series two years ago. But they fell out over plans for a third bid, with Ineos announcing last year that it had “reluctantly withdrawn its challenge” for the 2027 event in Naples. Ineos launched a legal action in March after expressing “surprise” that Ainslie’s Athena Racing had opted to keep using Britannia, which was beaten 7-2 by Emirates Team New Zealand in 2024, in the 2027 challenge. Court documents filed this year showed Ineos was claiming more than £10m for Athena’s alleged refusal to return the boat.

items.title: AI is reshaping banking jobs – but its ability to drive profits remains unclear
items.summary: Europe's banks are using AI to cut routine work, redeploy staff and hire more technical talent.
items.body: Banks' third-quarter results have brought their use of artificial intelligence into sharper focus, as lenders automate routine work, reshape hiring and test whether productivity gains can translate into revenue growth. This earnings season, Barclays unveiled layoffs in certain functions where AI is being deployed; while UniCredit and Santander said technology was freeing employees for higher-value work and improving processes. It comes as U.S. giants such as JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs make similar changes in staffing and workflows. But as banks pursue efficiency savings, strategists say evidence that AI is generating material, demonstrable revenue gains from it remains harder to pin down. UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel called AI an "opportunity to accelerate" that was allowing a shift toward more commercial, higher-value work and greater client engagement.

items.title: 'Break-in and rising costs could kill my business'
items.summary: Gordon Kidd says if things do not improve financially, he fears his firm in Shifnal will go under.
items.body: The owner of a cycle shop says he is considering closing the business after a break-in and soaring costs. Gordon Kidd, who runs Shifnal Cycles, estimates that a burglary last month cost him about £20,000 after three customer bikes and a frame were stolen and the subsequent repairs to his shop. Along with rising bills and a "lack of government support", the former armed forces veteran said the business in Shifnal may not be viable if financial pressures continue. A government spokesperson said that, from next year, businesses such as cycle shops would see their business rates either frozen, reduced or cut to zero, with half of the high-street retailers paying no rates. West Mercia Police said it had received a report of a burglary on 31 October, and an investigation was ongoing.

items.title: Anthropic recognises the risks to humanity – but is its governance really up to the job? | Nils Pratley
items.summary: The Claude AI developer’s unique setup is supposedly high-minded, but still represents extraordinary power concentration Boardroom governance matters, even in the world of big tech, it turns out. The business of how companies are run, investors are discovering, can be more…
items.body: B oardroom governance matters, even in the world of big tech, it turns out. The business of how companies are run, investors are discovering, can be more complicated than handing the founder or superstar chief executive as much control as he wants (it’s usually a he) and waiting for brilliant returns to appear. Sometimes a few checks on power are useful, especially when a crisis strikes. This revelation is no revelation at all, of course. For about 30 years until the first generation of big US tech companies came along, the thrust of corporate governance thinking was to insist on the basic fairness of the principle of “one share, one vote”. The owners should be able to chuck out misbehaving or underperforming managers by a simple majority, in other words.

items.title: China confirms Xi-Trump-Putin historic summit. What will be on the agenda?
items.summary: The talks are expected to focus on issues including nuclear non-proliferation, the Middle East war, trade policies and, possibly, the Ukraine war.
items.body: China confirmed Monday that President Xi Jinping will meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday, setting up the first-ever gathering of the three leaders. That confirmation from a spokesperson at China's Foreign Ministry follows announcements from Moscow and the White House. The Wall Street Journal had reported last month that Putin had proposed a three-way sit-down in an attempt to negotiate an end to the four-year war in Ukraine. While the summit among the three nations, on the sidelines of the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, is unprecedented, the leaders have held bilateral meetings over the years. Xi has met with Trump three times since October last year and more than 40 times with Putin since becoming president in 2013.

items.title: How Milburn won over Labour on tackling rising youth unemployment
items.summary: Labour grandee seems to have assuaged MPs’ nerves on need for welfare reform to tackle youth unemployment crisis In a boxing gym in Peterborough almost a year ago, Alan Milburn, freshly appointed to run a government review into the nearly 1 million young people out of work and…
items.body: In a boxing gym in Peterborough almost a year ago, Alan Milburn, freshly appointed to run a government review into the nearly 1 million young people out of work and education, said he would be “unafraid to shine a light on uncomfortable truths”. The Labour grandee, who held three cabinet jobs under Tony Blair, warned there was a “downward escalator” taking young people into a “world of benefits” and vowed to provide radical solutions. Many Labour MPs bristled. Just six months earlier, they had mounted a successful rebellion to kill off the government’s planned £5bn cuts to health and disability benefits, significantly damaging Keir Starmer’s political authority by forcing him into a U-turn on his flagship welfare bill.

items.title: Warren Buffett donates $5.5 billion, says kindness 'compounds' in Thanksgiving letter
items.summary: Following the donations, the chairman emeritus of Berkshire still owns 182,140 Class A shares -- roughly $162 billion.
items.body: Billionaire Warren Buffett donated Berkshire Hathaway shares worth about $5.5 billion to four philanthropic foundations, stepping up his annual charitable giving from the prior year. Buffett, 96, converted 6,150 Class A Berkshire shares into 9,225,000 Class B shares and gave 3,690,000 of those shares to The Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, and 1,845,000 shares each to The Sherwood Foundation, The Howard G. Buffett Foundation and NoVo Foundation — the foundations run by his three children, Susie, Howard and Peter Buffett. Following the donations, the chairman emeritus of Berkshire still owns 182,140 Class A shares — roughly $162 billion. "Last Thanksgiving I wrote that kindness is costless but also priceless.

items.title: Milburn’s historic report on Britain’s lost generation says one key thing: finally, young lives will really matter | Polly Toynbee
items.summary: The year-long Neets inquiry has yielded a slew of new policies. But what matters is the political and social priority shift designed to change this country This week marks a monumental turning point for young people in Britain: finally they will come first, not last. It will…
items.body: T his week marks a monumental turning point for young people in Britain: finally they will come first, not last. It will mark an end, we must hope, to a perverse system that casts down the future generation and overrewards the already privileged old. There are 1 million Neets (16- to 24-year-olds not in education, employment or training) in the UK, and they are partly George Osborne’s progeny. He targeted the young, tearing down the Connexions youth service , careers guidance, youth clubs, family benefits and further education funding. Michael Gove, with his Gradgrind exam fixation , scythed through music, sports, arts, drama and technology – subjects that kept many engaged with school. Remember the playing fields sold , the leisure centres closed , the mental health services for Covid-scarred children cut back .

items.title: OpenAI inks agreements with four independent evaluators to boost company's safety work
items.summary: Independent evaluators have taken on outsized importance following a series of high-profile AI safety and security incidents.
items.body: OpenAI on Monday announced it has signed agreements with four independent evaluators to help support the artificial intelligence company's safety work. The evaluators, Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire, will initially conduct distinct pilot assessments around model behavior and safeguards, OpenAI said. The company will give the organizations "deep access" to its internal systems as part of the agreements, adding that it plans to use what it learns to expand its work with independent experts going forward. "We expect this first phase of assessments to lead to longer-term, consistent embedded engagements over time that can continuously provide third party safety signals and recommended improvements on our most load bearing safety claims and safety cases," OpenAI said in a blog post .

items.summary: Predicting a final destination for reset negotiations between the EU and the UK is futile, given the wider challenges that Brussels is facing At the European Political Community summit in Dublin last week, Emmanuel Macron was pictured apparently waving a grinning Andy Burnham to…
items.body: A t the European Political Community summit in Dublin last week, Emmanuel Macron was pictured apparently waving a grinning Andy Burnham to a seat at the head of the table, as Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, looked on. It was the visual equivalent of the “ welcome back ” message delivered by the French president in the early autumn, following Mr Burnham’s suggestion that rejoining the EU was an option for the UK to consider. At the time, Le Monde was among the media outlets to try out an updated portmanteau to mark the moment; mercifully, “ Breturn ” has yet to catch on. By Friday, the mood music will be louder still. A long-awaited reset summit is due to deliver the first fruits of Mr Burnham’s ongoing rapprochement with Brussels, in the form of new deals on food and drink, and emissions trading.

items.title: Nvidia's Colette Kress confronts key questions in first earnings report since Jensen Huang’s exit
items.summary: Less than a week after Jensen Huang's abrupt departure, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress faces a major test with earnings.
items.body: Days after Jensen Huang's abrupt departure from the chipmaker he founded 33 years ago, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress will now face intense questions about what comes next. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly earnings after the close on Tuesday. While the company is again expected to show explosive growth as the key infrastructure provider to the artificial intelligence boom, Kress and her team will likely be forced to answer questions on chip sales to China, the risks tied to deals with neoclouds and what comes next under new leadership. Huang resigned Thursday, but Nvidia's legions of customers, partners and investors still rely on the company to continue shipping large quantities of graphics processing units and AI systems. Kress, who has been Nvidia's CFO since 2013, was tapped to lead the company while the board searches for a successor.

items.body: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh on Monday highlighted the potential economic benefits of artificial intelligence while warning that the emerging technology also could lead to widespread job losses or fail to deliver on its lofty expectations. Speaking in San Francisco before a blue-ribbon task force he assembled to examine productivity and employment, the central bank leader stressed that AI "will have significant impact on the economy, with important implications for monetary policy down the road." "I stress that while I'm not here to offer predictions, I'm not exactly impartial about American leadership in a time so filled with both challenge and possibility," he said in prepared remarks before his productivity and jobs task force.

items.title: Boots to begin prescribing medical cannabis in UK
items.summary: Online service will be offered to patients with eligible conditions, in a first for a British high street pharmacy Boots is to start prescribing medical cannabis, it has announced, in a first for a UK high street pharmacy. The online service is being offered to patients in the…
items.body: Boots is to start prescribing medical cannabis, it has announced, in a first for a UK high street pharmacy. The online service is being offered to patients in the UK aged 25 and older who have an eligible condition such as chronic pain, anxiety or insomnia. The chain is launching its SureLeaf service alongside a collaborative research programme with the University of Nottingham that will examine patient outcomes, prescribing practices and experience in the treatment of chronic pain. Patients will be invited to start an assessment online. Their suitability will then be reviewed by a clinical team, before they are invited to a video consultation with a consultant, according to Boots. Boots said any prescription would be “independently reviewed by a multidisciplinary clinical team that includes a second, independent consultant, before treatment begins”.

items.summary: PM to meet European leaders at summit this week aiming to secure agreements that ‘could raise GDP by 0.4%’ Andy Burnham will say on Monday that Brexit “has not worked” and that he will sign a new deal with the EU. It is the latest in a string of comments by the prime minister…
items.body: Andy Burnham will say on Monday that Brexit “has not worked” and that he will sign a new deal with the EU. It is the latest in a string of comments by the prime minister criticising Brexit, after he told the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday that the UK has “lost more than we gained” through leaving the EU. Burnham is due to meet European leaders at a summit this week and secure agreements that he says could raise GDP by 0.4% – about £17bn – including on food and farming, emissions trading and a youth mobility scheme. Speaking at the lord mayor’s banquet in the City of London, Burnham is expected to argue that Boris Johnson’s promise to take back control was not delivered, and that the country was left with a needlessly hard Brexit that created barriers for businesses and damaged its economic potential.

items.title: Cantwell urges Lutnick to stop AI chip sales to China ahead of Xi meeting
items.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has drawn fire for his close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the department's treatment of the company.
items.body: Sen. Maria Cantwell , the top Democrat on the Senate commerce committee, alleged in a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Sunday that the department under his leadership failed to prevent China from accessing the U.S.'s most advanced artificial intelligence chips. In the letter, Cantwell prodded Lutnick to enforce export controls and stop the flow of AI chips to companies barred from receiving the technology. She sent the missive ahead of a planned meeting this week between U.S. officials and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, in China. Her urging comes as Washington reels from revelations that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang. Nvidia is the leading U.S. company designing advanced AI chips.

items.title: Weakening UK electric vehicle targets would hurt car industry, ministers told
items.summary: Exclusive: Experts say watering down ZEV mandate would slow market and hamper efforts to reduce cost of living Moves to weaken the UK’s targets on electric vehicles would hurt the car industry as well as consumers, campaigners and experts have said before a key intervention from…
items.body: Moves to weaken the UK’s targets on electric vehicles would hurt the car industry as well as consumers, campaigners and experts have said before a key intervention from government advisers expected this week. The climate change committee (CCC) will write to ministers on Wednesday about the effects of changing the zero emissions vehicle (ZEV) mandate on the cost of living and the UK’s net zero targets. The current mandate stipulates that 80% of new car sales will have to be electric from 2030, and 100% from 2035, but it has been reported that Labour is poised to reduce those targets. Campaigners said the evidence to be examined by the CCC all pointed to consumers losing out from any weakening of the targets. The CCC has kept its deliberations under wraps, but its chair, Nigel Topping, has a long history of advocacy for electric vehicles.

items.title: ‘Standing on one leg’: IMF chief warns about global economy as AI circular financing hits $1 trillion
items.summary: Kristalina Georgieva says circular financing among AI companies has grown to just over $1 trillion, two-thirds of it debt, as investor enthusiasm cools
items.body: The global economy is "on the AI leg," International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said Monday, warning that the overdependence on the sector risks the world's financial stability. Georgieva flagged that a "sudden drop in investment confidence and withdrawal from the AI field" could weaken economic growth, speaking with CNBC's JP Ong on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' summit in the Philippines. "We have a world economy that is standing on one leg on the AI leg. If this leg wobbles, that can lead to financial stability troubles," Georgieva warned. Circular financing among AI companies — where money invested in an AI company ultimately flows back to the investor through purchase orders — has grown to a little over $1 trillion, two-thirds of it funded by debt, the IMF estimates.

items.title: Surge of US datacenters adds equivalent of Denmark’s annual emissions, study finds
items.summary: ‘Hyperscaler’ datacenters across country draw upon dirtier power sources to meet vast energy needs, research shows The frantic buildout of “hyperscaler” datacenters in the US has collectively caused planet-heating emissions of about the same scale as Denmark emits in a year, new…
items.body: The frantic buildout of “hyperscaler” datacenters in the US has collectively caused planet-heating emissions of about the same scale as Denmark emits in a year, new research has found. In that period, 403 “hyperscalers” – the largest datacenters used primarily to handle the growth of artificial intelligence – emitted about 25.7m metric tons of carbon dioxide, according to the study. This is equivalent to the entire annual carbon pollution of Denmark, a country of 6 million people, and is about two to three times more than a previous estimate of hyperscale emissions in 2018. The latest research, published in Nature Sustainability , found that these datacenters were responsible for about 1.8% of total US electricity consumption. Researchers said this vast datacenter energy demand, centered on states such as Virginia, Oregon, Ohio and Iowa, is almost certainly a conservative estimate.

items.title: Novo says Wegovy injection lowers BMI and obesity rates in children in trial
items.summary: Wegovy is already approved to treat obesity in children ages 12 and older, but there are currently no approved medications for those under 12.
items.body: Novo on Monday released full results from a late-stage trial showing its blockbuster Wegovy injection helped children ages 6 to under 12 with obesity shed weight, significantly lowering their body mass index. Wegovy reduced BMI by an estimated 19.7 percentage points on average compared with a placebo at 68 weeks, with BMI falling 17.4% among children receiving the drug and rising 2.2% among those receiving a placebo. Those results assumed patients stayed on treatment during the trial. When evaluating all children in the study, including those who discontinued treatment, Wegovy lowered BMI by an estimated average of 16.2 percentage points more than the placebo at 68 weeks. All 167 kids in the study received lifestyle modifications throughout the trial, including a ​reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.

items.body: The French Football Federation president, Philippe Diallo, has been confirmed as Uefa’s surprise late choice to run for the Fifa presidency. The search for a Uefa-backed candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino was taken to the wire, with Wednesday the deadline for those planning to contest the Fifa election in March. “At a meeting held today and chaired by Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin, the national associations represented on the Uefa executive committee and the Fifa council invited Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation (FFF), to stand as a candidate in the Fifa presidential election in March 2027 and unanimously pledged their full support,” a statement said. Diallo emerged as the favourite after plans to enlist a decorated former player or manager did not reach fruition.

items.title: Prediction market odds for Tesla-SpaceX merger by April 2027 top 60%
items.summary: The odds have climbed to 62% from 27% since Thursday, amid growing speculation that Musk's two companies will integrate.
items.body: Odds of a SpaceX and Tesla merger before March 2027 have climbed to 62% from 27% on Kalshi since Thursday. Chances that Elon Musk's two companies, SpaceX, a satellite and rocket maker, and Tesla, an electric vehicle manufacturer, will soon integrate have jumped since late last week across multiple Kalshi markets. The contract asks, "When will Tesla and SpaceX merge?" and would be verified by news outlets and the Securities and Exchange Commission's EDGAR database. On Friday, Walter Isaacson , a CNBC contributor and author of a Musk biography, told CNBC's " Squawk Box " he's confident a merger is coming. He cited Terafab, the semiconductor project involving Tesla, SpaceX and xAI, as a catalyst. Tesla's 2026 annual shareholder meeting, set for Dec. 3, may provide more insight into a potential linkup, Isaacson said.

items.title: Coles investigates cyber-attack and apologises to customers
items.summary: Supermarket giant says no customer, team or supplier data compromised but recommends updating passwords as a precaution Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australia’s second-largest retailer has been targeted in a cyber-attack, though it is still too…
items.body: Australia’s second-largest retailer has been targeted in a cyber-attack, though it is still too early to tell whether any of its data has been stolen or compromised. Coles revealed the threat on Monday morning, saying it was investigating with support from the Australian Cyber Security Centre and global security experts. “Coles Group Limited is currently investigating a cyber security incident,” the company said in a statement to the stock exchange. “We have not identified any evidence that customer, team or supplier data has been compromised or removed from Coles’ systems. “Operations continue and customers are able to shop as normal with Coles in stores and online.” Coles apologised to its customers for any concerns they might have at “a time of increasing cyber incidents in Australia and around the world”.

items.title: NATO member Estonia to close Russia border after attempted 'sabotage' of drone maker
items.summary: Estonia says closing the crossings would help curb hostile activity and sanctions circumvention.
items.body: NATO member Estonia says it is preparing to close road border crossings with Russia from Dec. 1, as it blames Moscow for an attempted "sabotage" of one of its defense companies. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on Sunday that Russia's military intelligence service GRU had ordered an arson attack against Estonian drone maker Threod Systems in the early hours of Saturday morning. Authorities said the attempted attack did not cause significant damage and eight people were detained in connection with it. Estonia, which shares a 294-kilometer (183-mile) border with Russia, said closing the crossings would help to reduce Moscow's ability to conduct hostile activities against it and mitigate risks related to sanctions circumvention.
